title: Mephibosheth
lead: Jonathan's son, lamed as a child, whom David brought to eat at his table for Jonathan's sake; his loyalty is later questioned in Absalom's revolt.

sections.b: Mephibosheth was five when news came of his father's death, and he was lamed when his nurse dropped him in flight (2 Samuel 4:4). David, keeping his oath to Jonathan (1 Samuel 20:14–17), restores Saul's land to him and seats him at the royal table (2 Samuel 9). During Absalom's revolt his servant Ziba accuses him of hoping for the throne (2 Samuel 16:1–4); when David returns, Mephibosheth says he was betrayed, and David divides the land (2 Samuel 19:24–30). David spares him when he hands Saul's other descendants to the Gibeonites (2 Samuel 21:7). Chronicles calls him Merib-baal (1 Chronicles 8:34; 9:40).
